prompt: Match each word to what it is.

pairs.right: The definition: an image and how to cut the work
One run of it, tonight's for instance
One piece of a run, with an index

prompt: What does Cloud Run read to decide whether a task succeeded?

choices.text: Whether an ERROR line was logged
choices.why: Logs are not read for the verdict.

choices.text: Whether the container answered on PORT
choices.why: A job has no port.

choices.text: The container's exit status, 0 or not
choices.why: Right. A failing job must exit non-zero.

choices.text: How long the task ran against its timeout
choices.why: A timeout fails a task; finishing early does not make it succeed.

prompt: A service answers a request at once and then spends two minutes generating a report in the background. What does the lesson call it?
hint: Who is waiting for the report?

choices.text: A job pretending to be a service
choices.why: Right. Work with an end and nobody waiting is a job.

choices.text: A well-designed service that keeps callers fast
choices.why: It relies on CPU after the response, which lesson 11 explains.

choices.text: A task with parallelism of one
choices.why: It is not a job at all, which is the problem.

choices.text: A service with a minimum instance
choices.why: Nothing says it has a minimum.

prompt: An execution of a job with --tasks=3 starts three ___, each told which piece it is.
With 3 tasks, which orders does task 1 take from ORDERS[index::count] over 1001 to 1010?

choices.why: That is task 0.
That is a range, not a stride.
That is task 2.
Right. The capture shows the same.

prompt: Ten orders are cut by stride across 3 tasks. How many orders does task 0 take?
Each task reads the orders from a database with SELECT id FROM orders WHERE day = yesterday, then takes its stride. What is missing?
hint: Is the list the same in every task?

choices.text: A LIMIT, so each task reads less
choices.why: Each still needs the whole list to take its stride.

choices.text: An ORDER BY
choices.why: Right. Without it the strides may overlap and leave gaps.

choices.text: A transaction around the read
choices.why: Isolation does not fix the order of rows.

choices.text: The task index in the WHERE clause
choices.why: That is the hash cut, a different method.

prompt: Why is --parallelism usually the number that protects something?

choices.text: It caps the number of tasks in the execution
choices.why: That is --tasks.

choices.text: It sets how many retries each task gets
choices.why: That is --max-retries.

choices.text: It caps load on whatever the tasks share
choices.why: Right. Three hundred at once can exhaust its connections.

choices.text: It lowers the price per task
choices.why: Price follows running time, not parallelism.

prompt: A job has 120 tasks of equal length and a parallelism of 8. About how many rounds does the execution take?
Task 1 fails on attempt 0. What is the retry?

choices.text: Same index, with the counter now at 1
choices.why: Right. Same index, next attempt.

choices.text: A new execution of the whole job
choices.why: Retries are per task.

choices.text: Task 1 again with the next index, 2
choices.why: The index does not change.

choices.text: Tasks 0, 1 and 2 again
choices.why: The others are not affected.

prompt: An attempt wrote invoices for 1002 and 1005 and then crashed. The retry writes all three. How do you keep each order at one invoice?
hint: Doing it twice should equal doing it once.

choices.text: Set parallelism to 1 so tasks never overlap
choices.why: The duplicate comes from the retry of one task, not from overlap.

choices.text: Raise the timeout so attempts never crash
choices.why: Crashes have other causes than time.

choices.text: Skip the orders logged in attempt 0
choices.why: Logs say what was planned, not what was written.

choices.text: Give each a fixed name, and overwrite on retry
choices.why: Right. The retry rewrites invoice-1002 instead of adding one.

prompt: A task has timeout = "600s" and max_retries = 3. In minutes, how long can it run in total before the execution fails?
hint: One attempt plus three retries, each ten minutes.

prompt: A job charges customers' cards and cannot be made idempotent. What does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: max_retries = 3, so a failed charge is completed
choices.why: It would charge cards that were already charged.

choices.text: max_retries = 0, and an alert when it fails
choices.why: Right. A retry would do harm.

choices.text: A longer timeout, so it never needs a retry
choices.why: Time does not prevent every failure.

choices.text: More tasks, so each failure affects fewer cards
choices.why: Smaller pieces still charge twice on retry.

prompt: An operation that leaves the same result when done twice is called ___.
In jobtf/main.tf there are two nested template blocks. What does the inner one describe?

choices.text: The schedule of the job
choices.why: A job has no schedule of its own.

choices.text: How many tasks run at once
choices.why: That is parallelism, in the outer block.

choices.text: How each single task runs
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The traffic split between revisions
choices.why: Jobs have no traffic.

prompt: What starts a Cloud Run job every night?
hint: A job has no schedule of its own.

choices.text: Cloud Scheduler, on a cron
choices.why: Right. An authorised API call on a cron expression.

choices.text: The job's own cron field
choices.why: There is no such field.

choices.text: A minimum instance that wakes it
choices.why: Jobs have no instances waiting.

choices.text: The metadata server of lesson 7
choices.why: That belongs to Compute Engine machines.

prompt: The scheduler job has schedule = "0 2 * * *" and no time_zone. When does it run for a shop in São Paulo?

choices.text: At 02:00 in São Paulo, the project's region
choices.why: The region does not set the time zone.

choices.text: At 02:00 in the time zone of whoever applied it
choices.why: Nobody's laptop decides it.

choices.text: It refuses to run until a time zone is set
choices.why: It runs, in UTC.

choices.text: At 02:00 UTC, which is 23:00 the day before in São Paulo
choices.why: Right. Before the day being invoiced has ended.

prompt: What role does the scheduler's service account need for the call to work?

choices.text: roles/owner on the project
choices.why: Far more than it needs.

choices.text: roles/run.invoker on the job
choices.why: Right. Granted on the job, in a real setup.

choices.text: roles/cloudscheduler.admin
choices.why: That administers schedules, not the job.

choices.text: No role: an OAuth token is enough on its own
choices.why: A token proves who calls, not what they may do.

prompt: Which habits keep a nightly job honest? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: An alert on a failed execution
choices.why: Right; a message in the morning.

choices.text: A way to run it by hand
choices.why: Right; for the morning the schedule failed.

choices.text: A schedule every minute, to catch up faster
choices.why: That invites overlapping executions.

choices.text: Idempotent writes, in case two executions overlap
choices.why: Right.

prompt: How many fields does the cron expression "0 2 * * *" have?
Put the night of the invoice job in order.
items: Cloud Scheduler fires at 02:00 São Paulo time
It POSTs to the job's :run method with its token
Cloud Run starts an execution of three tasks
Each task invoices its stride and exits 0
trap: The execution cannot start before the API call that asks for it.

prompt: A nightly export usually takes 20 minutes, is scheduled every 30, and one night takes 50 because the database was slow. What risk does that create?
hint: What starts while the first is still running?

choices.text: The second execution waits until the first ends
choices.why: Nothing in the schedule waits.

choices.text: Cloud Scheduler disables the job
choices.why: It keeps firing on schedule.

choices.text: Two executions work on the same rows at once
choices.why: Right. Only idempotent writes make that harmless.

choices.text: The first execution is killed at 30 minutes
choices.why: Its timeout, not the schedule, decides that.

prompt: The variable that tells a task which piece it is, counted from zero, is CLOUD_RUN_TASK____.
Why did the lesson run the three tasks one after another instead of together?
hint: What would the logs look like?

choices.text: So that their logs would not interleave
choices.why: Right. On Cloud Run they would run at the same time.

choices.text: Docker cannot run three containers at once
choices.why: It can; the choice was about reading.

choices.text: Cloud Run jobs always run tasks one at a time
choices.why: They run up to the parallelism at once.

choices.text: Because the stride only works sequentially
choices.why: The stride needs no order between tasks.

prompt: Which of these are good candidates for a Cloud Run job rather than a service? Choose all that apply.
hint: Has an end, and nobody waiting.

choices.text: A nightly export of orders
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The shop's /orders API
choices.why: Somebody waits for each answer.

choices.text: A database migration before a release
choices.why: Right; it runs once and ends.

choices.text: Resizing a batch of uploaded photos
choices.why: Right, when nobody waits on each one.
